REMINDERS. 

Final Instructions.—Put your 
Camp K number on all your 
goods. Be sure you get your 
Privilege Card and Badge before 
going to the station.

WHAT TO BRING. 

For a long stay. Two double 
blankets, pillow, toothbrush, 
toilet articles, Bible, pyjamas, 
gym suit, gym shoes, 2 pairs 
heavy boots, extra laces, pull- 
over sweater, raincoat, rubber 
sheet, 2 pairs long khaki pants, 
baseball gloves, etc., knife, hat- 
chet, camera, musical instru- 
ments, calico bag (20 x 30 in.), 
to protect city clothes. 


HIKES. 

Bring along a.tin cup, plate, 
knife, fork and spoon, also some 
straps for hiking. Everyone is 
expected to take at least an 
overnight hike. 


Bring some books. 


Learn to swim before going to 
Camp. Then you'll be allowed 
outside the “Crib.” 


LIFE-SAVING TESTS. 
Mr. A. W. Ross, of the Royal 
Life Saving Society, will again 
visit Camp to hold examina- 
tions. 


PHOTOGRAPHY. 

Three good prizes are offered 
for the best Nature Study, 
Landscape and Action pictures. 
Try for all three. 


KANAWANA. 


Year by year old campers have 
been returning to Kanawana 


’ prepared to do their full share in 


making Camp a success, bring- 
ing a smile, a cheerful word and 
a desire to get into everything, 
and to “Play the Game.” Come 
in this spirit and Kanawana will 
be to you, too, the Camp of fond 
memories.

KAMP KANAWANA 


is not a money-making venture. 
The Camp fee is kept as low as 
it can be in order to make Camp 
available to as many boys as pos- 
sible. Owned and operated by 
the Young Men’s Christian As- 
sociation of Montreal. 


GREAT ENGINEERING FEAT 


Removing the “Ritz.’’ This 
building in its time has served 
as hospital, library, barber shop 
and directors’ office. It will be 
moved to the brow of the hill 
between Tent A and Chute. 


A DAY’S DOINGS. 


7 A.M.— All up, setting-up 
drill, dip, tooth-brush parade, 
air bedding, flag raising, break- 
fast, chapel, Camp duties. 10 
A.M.—Badge work, instruction- 
al classes, swim, dinner at 1 
o’clock. Rest Hour. 2 P.M.— 
Short hikes, games, athletics, 
boating, ete. Swim, flag lower- 
ing, Supper, twilight baseball 
leagues, camp-fire, councils, en- 
tertainments, to the tents at 9 
p.m., tent devotions 9.20, lights 
out, quiet 9.30.

their white ducks.

SENIOR CABIN. 


Mr. R. L. Charlton reports 
that he hopes to complete ar- 
rangements for a Senior Log 
Cabin. On rainy nights the 
Cabin, with a roaring fire throw- 
ing out its warmth and comfort, 
will be more than welcome. 


COST. 

The cost is $8.50 per week 
This includes one return trip 
from Montreal to Camp. All 
financial arrangements must be 


made in advance. Talk it over 
with the Y.M.C.A. Secretary. 


CANOEING. 


Be sure to get your permit 
signed. 
Bring your paddle. 


VISITORS. 


The Camp Management prée- 
fers to know in advance if visit- 
ors are expected. Cost, 50¢ per 
night. For each meal, 50c. Rig 
to Piedmont from Camp, $1.50 
each way.

CAMP OTOREKE. 


During the season a 3 day 
Camp Trek will be held to the 
Y.M.C.A. camp at Ste. Adolphe 
de Howard. 


NOTE:—All baggage, blan- 
kets, pots & pans, ete., will be 
sent by express. 


CAMP OPENS JUNE 23. 
| CLOSES SEPT. 1.

Kanawana from the Water. 


During the season there will be a Central week-end, North Branch week-end, Westmount week-end, etc. Also 
branch stunt nights, special visitors at the Sunday services, and the Big Trek to Camp Otoreke, St. Adolphe de 
Howard, and other events that there isn’t space to tell about. Expected long-term Leaders: Mr. Guiton and 
other Secretaries, Mr. Clark, Mr. W. Stone, Ged. Merrit, Mr. F. Webb, Mr. Cousins, of Grand Mere, and others.
